candidate.text: Proposed uncertainty rule: use the district as the independent unit and a district-clustered sandwich covariance for the study's association coefficient estimator. All included people in the same district share one cluster; distinct districts are treated as independent. For unnormalised individual estimating contributions u_i and bread A (the negative derivative of their total estimating equation), form U_g = sum of u_i in district g and V = A^{-1} [sum over g of U_g U_g^T] A^{-T}. Use the unscaled large-cluster form (CR0, no finite-sample multiplier), SE_j = sqrt(V_jj), and two-sided 95% normal-Wald coefficient intervals beta_j ± 1.96 SE_j. If reporting a ratio fitted on a log scale, exponentiate that coefficient interval; do not exponentiate an additive-scale coefficient. These numerical conventions are explicit local proposals, not claims that the supplied note selects them. The approximation is proposed only for at least 40 independent districts actually contributing to the fitted estimator; the supplied design has 60. If a future fit/subset contributes fewer than 40, or the bread is singular, do not silently switch to ordinary errors: retain that fit as requiring a separate uncertainty-method assessment. Population inclusion, original time zero, follow-up, exposure/event attribution, point estimator and association estimand are not changed by this covariance decision. It consumes the fitted estimating contributions, bread and district membership; upstream cohort/model specifications and numerical implementation must be verified before any analysis. No data analysis is authorized by this candidate.

saved_items.why: I-000003: the two rules trade retained follow-up against a longer reverse-causation exclusion; zero present events in months 6–12 does not establish equivalence.

candidate.text: Proposed lag parameter: exclude the first 6 calendar months of otherwise eligible follow-up from the original person-specific follow-up start date t0. The operative inputs are t0 and the existing calendar-date eligible follow-up/event records. Define L as t0 plus 6 calendar months, using the same day of month, clamped to the last day of the target month if that day does not exist. Retain only otherwise eligible follow-up dates d with d >= L, subject to the unchanged overall follow-up end and existing event/risk-set eligibility. An otherwise eligible event on L is included; an event before L is excluded from the analyzed post-lag event set. If no eligible follow-up remains on or after L, that person contributes no post-lag information. Both events and eligible follow-up time before L are excluded; this is not merely a filter that removes early events while retaining their person-time. Original t0 and existing exposure attribution are unchanged; L is the start of retained follow-up, not a new exposure assignment. The target is the association in the eligible post-lag follow-up/event population, which may differ when the lag changes. This F specifies the lag filter only: upstream clinical cohort, t0 construction, event/risk-set eligibility and attribution must be specified separately before implementation, and are not invented here. The fully specified alternative replaces 6 by 12 in every part of this rule and leaves all other predicates identical. Six months is the proposed candidate, not a confirmed selection. Twelve months removes an additional possible reverse-causation interval but sacrifices otherwise usable follow-up; the source provides no quantitative bias reduction or universal optimum.
